questions.question: A family spends 30%, 20%, 17.5%, and 12.5%, of it's monthly income for house rent, food and medicines, education of children and entertainment, respectively. The remaining is divided for savings and donations in the ratio 3 : 2. The sum of the expenditure on house rent and education of children is ₹39,900. After one year if house rent and expenditure on entertainment are reduced by 5% and 2.5%, respectively, and expenditure on education of children is increased by 2.5% and the remaining expenditures except savings are same as the previous year, then what is the amount saved per month in the present year?
questions.questionHtml: A family spends 30%, 20%, 17.5%, and 12.5%, of it's monthly income for house rent, food and medicines, education of children and entertainment, respectively. The remaining is divided for savings and donations in the ratio 3 : 2. The sum of the expenditure on house rent and education of children is ₹39,900. After one year if house rent and expenditure on entertainment are reduced by 5% and 2.5%, respectively, and expenditure on education of children is increased by 2.5% and the remaining expenditures except savings are same as the previous year, then what is the amount saved per month in the present year?
questions.solution:
Let monthly income be I. House rent 30% plus education 17.5% equals 47.5% of I, and this sum is ₹39,900; hence I = 39,900 ÷ 0.475 = ₹84,000.

Base-year spends: rent = 30% of 84,000 = ₹25,200; food/medicines = 20% = ₹16,800; education = 17.5% = ₹14,700; entertainment = 12.5% = ₹10,500; remaining 20% split as savings:donations = 3:2 ⇒ savings = 12% = ₹10,080 and donations = 8% = ₹6,720.

Present year changes applied to last year’s amounts: rent ↓5% ⇒ 25,200×0.95 = ₹23,940; entertainment ↓2.5% ⇒ 10,500×0.975 = ₹10,237.5; education ↑2.5% ⇒ 14,700×1.025 = ₹15,067.5; food/medicines and donations unchanged at ₹16,800 and ₹6,720.

Present total (excluding savings) = 23,940 + 16,800 + 15,067.5 + 10,237.5 + 6,720 = ₹72,765; savings now = 84,000 − 72,765 = ₹11,235 per month.

questions.question: There are three containers, X, Y and Z, each having a solution of concentrated juice, sugar solution and water. The concentrated juice is 5% in each whereas the sugar solution is 70%, 60% and 50%, respectively and the rest is water. Solutions in X, Y and Z are mixed together in a bigger drum. Ten litres are drawn from the drum and poured in to a bucket to which 2 litres water is added. Find the percentage of sugar solution in the bucket.
questions.questionHtml: There are three containers, X, Y and Z, each having a solution of concentrated juice, sugar solution and water. The concentrated juice is 5% in each whereas the sugar solution is 70%, 60% and 50%, respectively and the rest is water. Solutions in X, Y and Z are mixed together in a bigger drum. Ten litres are drawn from the drum and poured in to a bucket to which 2 litres water is added. Find the percentage of sugar solution in the bucket.
questions.solution:
Let each container contribute equal volume when mixed; then the sugar-solution percentage in the drum is the weighted average of 70%, 60%, and 50%, so drum sugar% = (70 + 60 + 50)/3 = 60% by the mixture/weighted-average rule.

Drawn 10 L from the drum contains sugar solution = 60% of 10 L = 6 L.

After adding 2 L water, total volume = 12 L; sugar amount unchanged, so new sugar% = 6/12 = 50% by dilution (C2 = C1 × V1/V2).

questions.question: In a company, employees are divided into three levels: Junior, Mid and Senior. The average salary of the company is ₹47,500. Juniors earn ₹30,000 on average, Seniors earn ₹80,000, and there are 5 mid-level employees earning ₹50,000 each. If the number of Junior employees is twice that of Seniors, then what will be the average salary of the company after 4 juniors left the company and 2 mid-level and 3 senior level new employees join the company (to the nearest whole number)?
questions.questionHtml: In a company, employees are divided into three levels: Junior, Mid and Senior. The average salary of the company is ₹47,500. Juniors earn ₹30,000 on average, Seniors earn ₹80,000, and there are 5 mid-level employees earning ₹50,000 each. If the number of Junior employees is twice that of Seniors, then what will be the average salary of the company after 4 juniors left the company and 2 mid-level and 3 senior level new employees join the company (to the nearest whole number)?
questions.solution:
Let Seniors = s, Juniors = 2s, and Mid-level = 5 initially.
Initial headcount = 3s + 5 and initial total salary = 30,000·(2s) + 80,000·s + 50,000·5 = 140,000s + 250,000.
Given average 47,500: (140,000s + 250,000)/(3s + 5) = 47,500 ⇒ 140,000s + 250,000 = 142,500s + 237,500 ⇒ s = 5.
Thus Juniors = 10, Mid = 5, Seniors = 5, total = 20, and the check gives average = 950,000/20 = 47,500.
After changes: 4 juniors leave ⇒ Juniors = 6; 2 mid join ⇒ Mid = 7; 3 seniors join ⇒ Seniors = 8; new total = 21.
New total salary = 6·30,000 + 7·50,000 + 8·80,000 = 180,000 + 350,000 + 640,000 = 1,170,000.
New average = 1,170,000/21 ≈ ₹55,714 (nearest whole number).

questions.question: A student takes 4 subjects in a year, the weights and marks for the first semester is as below. Subject Weights Marks Math 0.3 85 History 0.2 90 Chemistry 0.4 78 English 0.1 95 In the second semester, the student scored 5 more marks each in Math and Chemistry and 5 less marks each in History and English, the weights remaining the same. What is the overall average for the year?

In the second semester, the student scored 5 more marks each in Math and Chemistry and 5 less marks each in History and English, the weights remaining the same. What is the overall average for the year?
questions.solution:
Semester 1 weighted average = 0.3×85 + 0.2×90 + 0.4×78 + 0.1×95 = 84.2.

Semester 2 marks: Math 90, History 85, Chemistry 83, English 90 (weights unchanged) ⇒ weighted average = 0.3×90 + 0.2×85 + 0.4×83 + 0.1×90 = 86.2.

Overall yearly average = average of the two semester weighted scores since semesters carry equal total weight = (84.2 + 86.2)/2 = 85.2.

questions.question: Let a, b and c be natural numbers. If the average value of 20% of a and 30% of b is 270; that of 10% of b and 25% of c is 115 and the difference between b and c is 200, then what is the value of (a + b + 2c)?
questions.questionHtml: Let a, b and c be natural numbers. If the average value of 20% of a and 30% of b is 270; that of 10% of b and 25% of c is 115 and the difference between b and c is 200, then what is the value of (a + b + 2c)?
questions.solution:
From “average of 20% of a and 30% of b is 270”: (0.2a + 0.3b)/2 = 270 ⇒ 0.2a + 0.3b = 540 ⇒ 2a + 3b = 5400 using the average and percent-of formulas.

From “average of 10% of b and 25% of c is 115”: (0.1b + 0.25c)/2 = 115 ⇒ 0.1b + 0.25c = 230 ⇒ 10b + 25c = 23000 ⇒ 2b + 5c = 4600 by multiplying both sides.

Given |b − c| = 200; try b = c + 200 in 2b + 5c = 4600 ⇒ 2(c + 200) + 5c = 4600 ⇒ 7c = 4200 ⇒ c = 600, b = 800 (the other sign gives a non-integer).

From 2a + 3b = 5400 ⇒ 2a + 2400 = 5400 ⇒ 2a = 3000 ⇒ a = 1500.

Therefore, a + b + 2c = 1500 + 800 + 1200 = 3500.

questions.question: During a new year, a father gives 25% of his fortune to each of his four sons A, B, C and D. They all invest, and at the end of the 1ˢᵗ year, A and B each earn a profit of 40%, whereas C and D make a loss of 20% and 30%, respectively. At the end of the second year, (reinvesting any profit made) A makes a loss of 50%, whereas B, C and D make a profit of 25% each. What percentage of their father's fortune is left at the end of the second year (rounded off to nearest integer)?
questions.questionHtml: During a new year, a father gives 25% of his fortune to each of his four sons A, B, C and D. They all invest, and at the end of the 1ˢᵗ year, A and B each earn a profit of 40%, whereas C and D make a loss of 20% and 30%, respectively. At the end of the second year, (reinvesting any profit made) A makes a loss of 50%, whereas B, C and D make a profit of 25% each. What percentage of their father's fortune is left at the end of the second year (rounded off to nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
Let father’s fortune be F; each son receives 25% of F, so each starts with 0.25F and successive gains/losses apply multiplicatively to his own amount.

End of Year 1: A = 0.25F × 1.40 = 0.35F; B = 0.25F × 1.40 = 0.35F; C = 0.25F × 0.80 = 0.20F; D = 0.25F × 0.70 = 0.175F; total = 0.35F + 0.35F + 0.20F + 0.175F = 1.075F.

End of Year 2 (reinvesting): A = 0.35F × 0.50 = 0.175F; B = 0.35F × 1.25 = 0.4375F; C = 0.20F × 1.25 = 0.25F; D = 0.175F × 1.25 = 0.21875F; total = 0.175F + 0.4375F + 0.25F + 0.21875F = 1.08125F ≈ 108.125% of F.

Rounded to the nearest integer, the percentage of the father’s fortune left is 108%.

questions.question: A dealer buys two articles X and Y for ₹5,500 each. He marks each of them at the same price. He sells X by giving two successive discounts of 55% and 60% and still earns ₹143 as profit. If he sells Y at a single discount of 76%, then what is the profit percentage on Y?
questions.questionHtml: A dealer buys two articles X and Y for ₹5,500 each. He marks each of them at the same price. He sells X by giving two successive discounts of 55% and 60% and still earns ₹143 as profit. If he sells Y at a single discount of 76%, then what is the profit percentage on Y?
questions.solution:
Cost price (CP) of each article = ₹5,500.

For X: profit = ₹143 ⇒ selling price SP_X = 5,500 + 143 = ₹5,643.

Two successive discounts of 55% and 60% leave a payable fraction (1 − 0.55)( 1 − 0.60) = 0.45 × 0.40 = 0.18 of the marked price (MP), so SP_X = 0.18 × MP ⇒ MP = 5,643 ÷ 0.18 = ₹31,350.

For Y: single discount of 76% leaves 24%, so SP_Y = 0.24 × 31,350 = ₹7,524.

Profit on Y = 7,524 − 5,500 = ₹2,024; profit% on Y = (2,024/5,500) × 100 = 36.8%.

questions.question: An item is initially sold at ₹500. Its price is first increased by 20% due to a surge in demand. After that, a 10% festive markdown is applied on the increased price. Following this, a 5% seasonal discount is applied on the new reduced price. However, before final billing, a service charge of 2% is added on the discounted price, and GST at 12% is levied on the amount after adding the service charge. What is the net change in the final billed price (after all taxes and charges) compared to the original price of ₹500 (correct to 2 decimal place)?
questions.questionHtml: An item is initially sold at ₹500. Its price is first increased by 20% due to a surge in demand. After that, a 10% festive markdown is applied on the increased price. Following this, a 5% seasonal discount is applied on the new reduced price. However, before final billing, a service charge of 2% is added on the discounted price, and GST at 12% is levied on the amount after adding the service charge. What is the net change in the final billed price (after all taxes and charges) compared to the original price of ₹500 (correct to 2 decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Start price: ₹500.

After +20% demand surge: 500×1.20=600500×1.20=600.

After −10% festive markdown: 600×0.90=540600×0.90=540.

After −5% seasonal discount: 540×0.95=513540×0.95=513.

Add service charge +2% before GST: 513×1.02=523.26513×1.02=523.26.

Add GST +12% on amount after service charge: 523.26×1.12=586.0512⇒523.26×1.12=586.0512⇒ ₹586.05 (rounded to 2 decimals).

Net change vs original ₹500: 586.05−500=86.05586.05−500=86.05 increase

questions.question: A dealer buys two articles X and Y for ₹1,500 each. He marks each of them at the same price. He sells X by giving two successive discounts of 25% and 44% and still earns ₹279 as profit. If he sells Y at a single discount of 58%, then what is the profit percentage on Y?
questions.questionHtml: A dealer buys two articles X and Y for ₹1,500 each. He marks each of them at the same price. He sells X by giving two successive discounts of 25% and 44% and still earns ₹279 as profit. If he sells Y at a single discount of 58%, then what is the profit percentage on Y?
questions.solution:
Cost price of each article (X and Y): CP = ₹1500.

For X, profit = ₹279 ⇒ selling price SP_X = 1500 + 279 = ₹1779.

Successive discounts 25% and 44% leave a fraction (1 − 0.25)( 1 − 0.44) = 0.75 × 0.56 = 0.42 of the marked price MP, so SP_X = 0.42 × MP ⇒ MP = 1779/0.42.

For Y, a single discount of 58% leaves (1 − 0.58) = 0.42 of MP, so SP_Y = 0.42 × MP = SP_X = ₹1779.

Profit on Y = 1779 − 1500 = ₹279, so profit% on Y = (279/1500) × 100 = 18.6%.

questions.question: P and Q work together to tile a floor of dimension of 16 m by 12 m, each tile being 1 m by 0.5 m. P can tile at the rate of 50 per hour and Q at 60 per hour. What is the time (in hours) taken to complete, if they work together?
questions.questionHtml: P and Q work together to tile a floor of dimension of 16 m by 12 m, each tile being 1 m by 0.5 m. P can tile at the rate of 50 per hour and Q at 60 per hour. What is the time (in hours) taken to complete, if they work together?
questions.solution:
Floor area = 16 × 12 = 192 m²; tile area = 1 × 0.5 = 0.5 m² ⇒ number of tiles needed = 192 / 0.5 = 384 tiles.

Rates: P = 50 tiles/hour, Q = 60 tiles/hour ⇒ combined rate = 50 + 60 = 110 tiles/hour.

Time together = total tiles / combined rate = 384 / 110 = 3.4909… hours ≈ 3.49 hours.

questions.question: A can beat B in a race of 800 m by 72 m or 12 seconds. Find the speed of A (in km/hr, rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.questionHtml: A can beat B in a race of 800 m by 72 m or 12 seconds. Find the speed of A (in km/hr, rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
“A beats B by 72 m or 12 s” means B covers 72 m in 12 s, so B’s speed = 72/12 = 6 m/s.

When A finishes 800 m, B has run 728 m; thus A : B = 800 : 728 = 100 : 91.

Hence A = (100/91) × B = (100/91) × 6 = 600/91 ≈ 6.5934 m/s.

Convert to km/h: A ≈ 6.5934 × 3.6 ≈ 23.74 km/h (rounded to two decimals).

questions.question: Let k be a natural number and 1 ≤ k ≤ 16. Let A be a set of two-digit natural numbers which are in the form 6k + 1, B be the set of two-digit prime numbers which are in the form 6k + 1, n(A) = x, n(B) = y, and the number of pairs of co-prime numbers of set A be z. What is the value of x + y + z?
questions.questionHtml: Let k be a natural number and 1 ≤ k ≤ 16. Let A be a set of two-digit natural numbers which are in the form 6k + 1, B be the set of two-digit prime numbers which are in the form 6k + 1, n(A) = x, n(B) = y, and the number of pairs of co-prime numbers of set A be z. What is the value of x + y + z?
questions.solution:
A consists of two-digit numbers of the form 6k+1 with 1 ≤ k ≤ 16; since 6·1+1=7 is not two-digit, take k=2,…,16 giving A = {13,19,25,31,37,43,49,55,61,67,73,79,85,91,97}, so x = n(A) = 15 using the arithmetic progression idea with d = 6.

B consists of the primes in this list; using the primes up to 100, the primes here are {13,19,31,37,43,61,67,73,79,97}, so y = 10.

Non-coprime pairs in A occur only when two numbers share a common prime factor; the only shared factors are 5 among {25,55,85} (3 pairs), 7 between {49,91} (1 pair), and 13 between {13,91} (1 pair), so non-coprime pairs = 5 and coprime pairs z = C( 15,2) − 5 = 105 − 5 = 100.

Therefore x + y + z = 15 + 10 + 100 = 125.

questions.question: The number of prime numbers lying between 333 and 346 is:
questions.questionHtml: The number of prime numbers lying between 333 and 346 is:
questions.solution:
Check integers strictly between 333 and 346: 334, 335, 336, 337, 338, 339, 340, 341, 342, 343, 344, 345.

Eliminate even numbers and multiples of 5: 334, 336, 338, 340, 342, 344 are composite; 335 and 345 are multiples of 5.

Test the remaining 337, 341, 343 by trial division up to √346 < 19 using primes 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17:

337 is not divisible by 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 ⇒ prime.

341 = 11 × 31 ⇒ composite.

343 = 7 × 49 ⇒ composite.

Hence primes in the interval are {337} only? Wait, also check 339 (3×113) composite ; 341 composite; 343 composite. But 347 and 349 are outside the open interval (333, 346). So primes are 337 only? No—also 331 and 347 are outside. Check 343 composite, 341 composite, 337 prime . Count = 1? However 339 composite . The primes strictly between 333 and 346 are 337 only, so total = 1.

questions.question: Five consecutive prime numbers A, B, C, D and E are in ascending order. If product of A × C × E = 1729 and product of B × C × D = 2431, find the next prime number to E.
questions.questionHtml: Five consecutive prime numbers A, B, C, D and E are in ascending order. If product of A × C × E = 1729 and product of B × C × D = 2431, find the next prime number to E.
questions.solution:
Factorize the given products: 1729=7×13×191729=7×13×19 and 2431=11×13×172431=11×13×17, so the common middle prime is C=13 C =13.
Thus A,C,E A , C , E match 7,13,197,13,19 and B,C,D B , C , D match 11,13,1711,13,17, giving consecutive primes A<B<C<D<E=7,11,13,17,19 A < B < C < D < E =7,11,13,17,19.
Hence E=19 E =19 and the next prime after 19 is 23.

questions.question: A school has less than 2000 students. If the students are divided in to groups of 9 or 12 or 20 exactly three are always left, but when divided into groups of 21, none are left out. Find the maximum number of groups that can be formed with 10 students in a group.
questions.questionHtml: A school has less than 2000 students. If the students are divided in to groups of 9 or 12 or 20 exactly three are always left, but when divided into groups of 21, none are left out. Find the maximum number of groups that can be formed with 10 students in a group.
questions.solution:
Since the same remainder 3 appears for divisors 9, 12, and 20, any valid student count must be of the form N = LCM( 9,12,20) × t + 3 = 180t + 3 using the shortcut “same remainder ⇒ LCM + remainder” pattern.

Also N must be divisible by 21. Try the smallest N in this family that is a multiple of 21: 180t + 3 ≡ 0 (mod 21) ⇒ 180 ≡ 12 (mod 21), so 12t ≡ 18 (mod 21) ⇒ divide by 3: 4t ≡ 6 (mod 7) ⇒ t ≡ 6 × 4 ^{ -1} ≡ 6 × 2 ≡ 12 ≡ 5 (mod 7), hence t = 5, 12, 19, …

t = 5 gives N = 180×5 + 3 = 903 (< 2000); the next t = 12 gives 2163 (> 2000), so N = 903 is the only feasible total.

Maximum 10-student groups = floor( 903/10) = 90.

questions.question: The average age of a family of n members is 25 years. If the age of the youngest member is 10 years, and the ratio of the average age of the remaining (n−1) members just before the birth of the youngest member to the current average age of (n−1) the oldest members is 2 : 3, then what is the value of 9n − n²?
questions.questionHtml: The average age of a family of n members is 25 years. If the age of the youngest member is 10 years, and the ratio of the average age of the remaining (n−1) members just before the birth of the youngest member to the current average age of (n−1) the oldest members is 2 : 3, then what is the value of 9n − n²?
questions.solution:
Current average age of n members = 25 ⇒ current total age S = 25n by the average formula.

Youngest is 10, so current sum of the oldest (n−1) members = S − 10 = 25n − 10.

Just before the youngest was born (10 years ago), each of these (n−1) members was 10 years younger, so their past sum = (25n − 10) − 10(n−1) = 15n; hence their past average = 15n/(n−1).

Current average of the oldest (n−1) = (25n − 10)/(n−1). The given ratio of past average to current average is 2:3, so 15 n : (25n − 10) = 2 : 3 ⇒ 45n = 50n − 20 ⇒ n = 4.

Therefore, 9n − n² = 9(4) − 4² = 36 − 16 = 20, which corresponds to 5n among the options.

questions.question: For which values of A and B does the given pair of linear equations 3x + 2y = 8 and (A − B)x + (A + B)y = 3A + B − 5 have an infinite number of solutions?
questions.questionHtml: For which values of A and B does the given pair of linear equations 3x + 2y = 8 and (A − B)x + (A + B)y = 3A + B − 5 have an infinite number of solutions?
questions.solution:
For two linear equations a1x + b1y = c1 and a2x + b2y = c2 to have infinitely many solutions, the proportionality condition must hold: a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2.

Here the equations are 3x + 2y = 8 and (A − B)x + (A + B)y = 3A + B − 5, so enforce 3 /( A − B) = 2 /( A + B) = 8 /( 3A + B − 5).

From 3 /( A − B) = 2 /( A + B) obtain 3(A + B) = 2(A − B) ⇒ A + 5B = 0 ⇒ A = −5B.

From 3 /( A − B) = 8 /( 3A + B − 5) obtain 3(3A + B − 5) = 8(A − B) ⇒ A + 11B = 15.

Solving A = −5B and A + 11B = 15 gives B = 5/2 and A = −25/2, and denominators A − B, A + B, 3A + B − 5 are nonzero, so the proportionality is valid.

questions.question: The cost of 13 pens and 3 notebooks is ₹234. If the cost of a pen decreases by ₹6 and the cost of a notebook increases by ₹9, then the cost of 16 pens and 2 notebooks is ₹144. What is the original cost of 6 pens and 17 notebooks?
questions.questionHtml: The cost of 13 pens and 3 notebooks is ₹234. If the cost of a pen decreases by ₹6 and the cost of a notebook increases by ₹9, then the cost of 16 pens and 2 notebooks is ₹144. What is the original cost of 6 pens and 17 notebooks?
questions.solution:
Let the original prices be p (per pen) and n (per notebook).
From the first condition: 13p + 3n = 234.
After changes: pen becomes p − 6 and notebook becomes n + 9; so 16(p − 6) + 2(n + 9) = 144 ⇒ 16p + 2n = 222 ⇒ 8p + n = 111.
Solve the system {13p + 3n = 234, 8p + n = 111}: from the second, n = 111 − 8p; substitute in the first ⇒ 13p + 3(111 − 8p) = 234 ⇒ 13p + 333 − 24p = 234 ⇒ −11p = −99 ⇒ p = 9; hence n = 111 − 72 = 39.
Required original cost = 6p + 17n = 6×9 + 17×39 = 54 + 663 = 717.

questions.question: Ten years back, the average age of a father and a son was 16 years and after 20 years, the average age of father and three times the age of son will be 78. What is the difference of their present ages?
questions.questionHtml: Ten years back, the average age of a father and a son was 16 years and after 20 years, the average age of father and three times the age of son will be 78. What is the difference of their present ages?
questions.solution:
Let present ages be F (father) and S (son).
Ten years ago, the average was 16 ⇒ (F − 10 + S − 10)/2 = 16 ⇒ F + S = 52.
After 20 years, the average of father and three times the son is 78 ⇒ (F + 20 + 3(S + 20))/2 = 78 ⇒ F + 3S + 80 = 156 ⇒ F + 3S = 76.
Solve: subtract the first from the second ⇒ (F + 3S) − (F + S) = 76 − 52 ⇒ 2S = 24 ⇒ S = 12; then F = 52 − 12 = 40.
Difference of present ages = F − S = 40 − 12 = 28 years.
